purpose: dipankarsarkar (round 41): guards against ADDING a word-boundary delimiter (e.g. ' and ', ' to ', ' of ') to the anchor, symmetric to round 36's FIXTURE-over-split-guard (which guards single-character delimiters). Built against a real, currently-inert hazard: ANTHROPIC-2026-deepseek-distillation-relay's source_locator opens with a PDF title containing the word 'and' ("Detecting and countering misuse of AI"), unrelated to any delimiter role. Today that record has no repo-host citation so the hazard never fires -- but the day its citation gains a real extracted-file path (this project already text-extracts PDFs with pypdf, per that record's own source_locator), a word-rung on 'and' would truncate the head at the title and silently flip source_structured from True to False. This fixture reproduces that exact shape now, before the real citation exists, so the rung stays caught if anyone adds it. Tested independently before shipping: reproduces exit 0 today (no word-rung exists), and flips to exit 1 the moment a word-boundary split on 'and', 'to', or 'of' is added -- confirmed on this fixture specifically, not assumed from the punctuation-rung fixtures. One correction to the round-41 message this fixture responds to: 'see' was proposed as a safe word alongside 'then', 'with', 'plus', etc. -- it is not. 'see' already breaks the existing FIXTURE-over-split-guard (round 36), whose source_locator opens with the literal word 'see'. Verified by running, not by re-reading the proposal.
